chapterTitle: FBISE Section A Board Examination Simulator 03
subject: english-9

questions.question: Which of the following words is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: 'Conscientious' is correctly spelled with 'scien' and suffix 'tious'.

questions.question: Identify the type of conditional: 'If water reaches 100°C, it boils.'
questions.explanation: Zero conditional expresses universal truths or scientific facts using present simple in both clauses.

questions.question: Identify the figure of speech: 'As brave as a lion.'
questions.explanation: Comparison using 'as ... as' constitutes a direct simile.

questions.question: Choose the correct voice: 'They will announce the board examination results tomorrow.'

options.A: The board examination results will be announced tomorrow.
options.B: The board examination results will have been announced tomorrow.
options.C: The board examination results are announced tomorrow.
options.D: The board examination results were announced tomorrow.

questions.explanation: Future simple 'will announce' converts to 'will be announced' in the passive voice.

questions.question: Identify the underlined verbal: 'To err is human; to forgive, divine.'
questions.explanation: 'To err' and 'to forgive' are bare 'to + base verb' infinitives functioning as nouns.

questions.question: Which sentence contains a relative pronoun?

options.A: The scientist whose discovery won the Nobel Prize gave a lecture.
options.B: This is the most memorable day of my life.
options.C: Everyone should do their duty diligently.
options.D: She herself designed the website layout.

questions.explanation: 'Whose' acts as a possessive relative pronoun connecting the dependent adjective clause.

questions.question: Identify the transitional device indicating result or cause-and-effect:
questions.explanation: 'Therefore' signifies a logical conclusion, result, or consequence.

questions.question: Identify the noun phrase in: 'The exceptionally talented young artist won the first prize.'
questions.explanation: 'The exceptionally talented young artist' consists of the noun head 'artist' with all its determiners and modifiers.

questions.question: In poetry, the repetition of initial consonant sounds in neighboring words is called:
questions.explanation: Alliteration is the deliberate repetition of identical initial consonant sounds in successive words.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'Neither the teacher nor the students ___ present yesterday.'
questions.explanation: With 'neither ... nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject ('students' -> plural 'were').

questions.question: Which of the following contains an abstract noun?

options.A: Honesty is the foundation of all righteous character.
options.C: The river flows down the valley.

questions.explanation: 'Honesty' is an intangible virtue and quality, qualifying as an abstract noun.

questions.question: Identify the preposition of time in: 'We will meet at sunset near the river.'
questions.explanation: 'At' introduces the specific point in time ('sunset').

questions.question: Which of the following is a compound sentence?

options.A: The bell rang, and the students entered the examination hall.
options.B: When the bell rang, the students entered the hall.
options.C: Upon the ringing of the bell, the students entered.
options.D: The students entered the examination hall after hearing the bell.

questions.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by coordinating conjunction 'and' form a compound sentence.

questions.question: Identify the correct article: 'He is ___ heir to a vast ancestral estate.'
questions.explanation: 'Heir' begins with a silent 'h' and vowel sound, requiring the indefinite article 'an'.

questions.question: Identify the literary device: 'I have told you a million times to double-check your calculations.'
questions.explanation: 'A million times' is an intentional extreme exaggeration used for rhetorical effect, known as hyperbole.
